repo_notes.content: Generate the wiki for Perseus MCP version 1.1.0 (published to PyPI as perseus-mcp 1.1.0 on 2026-11-12, following 1.0.0, 1.0.1 and 1.0.2). Treat pyproject.toml as the canonical version source. Describe 1.1.0 as a minor release in the 1.x line: it carries client-visible refinements to the discovery and pagination response contract together with reliability, test coverage, documentation, packaging, CI and release-process work. Do not invent a changelog. Verify individual changes against git history between the v1.0.2 and v1.1.0 tags, any CHANGELOG or release notes in the repository, the current source and the tests, and describe only what those confirm. Do not carry over 1.0.2 wording (patch release, thirteen tools, three workflows, old notebook counts) from earlier generated wiki text.

Use the current src-layout package: the implementation is in src/perseus_mcp/server.py, the package entry point is perseus_mcp.server:main, and the supported launch commands are the perseus-mcp console command, python -m perseus_mcp (src/perseus_mcp/__main__.py) and uv run perseus-mcp. There is no supported root-level server.py launcher. The package is published on PyPI (pip install perseus-mcp, Python >=3.11, optional extras docs and dev), so document PyPI installation as available; if README.md still says 'once a release is published', treat that wording as lagging the published package rather than as a limitation. Derive tool names and counts from the registered FastMCP tools in the current source; the current README documents 23 tools grouped into passage/navigation, discovery, search, Scaife retrieval, and cache management.

Pagination contract: README.md documents that list_text_groups and find_author_names return total_count (all matches before paging), returned_count (entries on the current page) and has_more, navigated with offset and limit (limit 1-500), and that the redundant match_count field has been removed in favor of total_count. Confirm this in src/perseus_mcp/server.py and tests/test_exploration_tools.py, then document it once in the discovery tool page and call it out with migration guidance on the release page. Also document that list_text_groups, find_author_names, get_author_resources and get_work_resources treat language as a real work-language filter, whereas search_perseus uses language only for query normalization and does not send it to Scaife as a corpus filter. find_author_names merges the legacy CTS inventory with the Scaife library catalog so Scaife-only authors such as Philo Judaeus remain discoverable. When author resolves to exactly one CTS textgroup, search_perseus sends it to Scaife as a server-side text_group filter; ambiguous matches fall back to local CTS URN-prefix filtering of the returned page.

Clearly distinguish local stdio clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code via claude mcp add perseus -- uv --directory /full/path/to/Perseus-mcp run perseus-mcp, Cursor, Windsurf, MCP Inspector, generic MCP clients) from ChatGPT: the checked-in server runs over stdio, while ChatGPT requires a separately deployed HTTPS /mcp endpoint and cannot launch the local command directly. Treat OpenRouter as an optional notebook-based LLM integration that requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY; the MCP server and its Perseus/Scaife upstream calls do not require that key. Explain that Perseus CTS and Scaife are separate upstream services whose inventories and edition URNs can differ, and that the live CTS service can return malformed HTML for GetFirstUrn and GetPrevNextUrn, which the tools recover from by deriving results from GetValidReff. The server currently exposes upstream HTTP errors (including 429 Too Many Requests) instead of retrying automatically.

Metadata cache: document PERSEUS_MCP_CACHE_DIR, PERSEUS_MCP_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 86400 seconds) and PERSEUS_MCP_DISABLE_CACHE=1, the default .cache/perseus-mcp location relative to the process working directory (so notebooks run from examples/ would otherwise use examples/.cache/perseus-mcp), the in-memory layer, atomic disk writes through unique sibling temporary files, safe sharing between local processes, and MetadataCacheWarning on disk-write failures that do not discard a fetched upstream response. Keep the metadata cache distinct from the shared in-process httpx client.

CI and release automation: derive the details from every file under .github/workflows/ and from Dependabot configuration rather than from memory. README.md currently describes tests.yml (pytest on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, fail-fast false, docs-only changes excluded), package.yml (python -m build and twine check, python-package artifact), secret-scan.yml (rejects tracked OpenRouter keys without printing them), codeql.yml (Python and GitHub Actions analysis on pushes to main and development, pull requests and weekly), dependency-review.yml (fails pull requests that add moderate-or-higher known vulnerabilities), weekly Dependabot checks for Python and GitHub Actions dependencies, release.yml (v* tags, tag must equal v<project.version>, builds and validates artifacts, creates the GitHub release, dispatches the PyPI workflow), publish.yml (tag-only, repeats the tag/version check, rebuilds, publishes through PyPI trusted publishing with OIDC and the protected pypi environment) and pages.yml (Jekyll build of docs/, deployed to GitHub Pages from main or master, validation-only builds on pull requests). Do not claim a linting workflow unless one exists in the repository. PyPI 1.1.0 files carry publish attestations signed by GitHub Actions; mention provenance only as far as the workflows and PyPI metadata support it.

Prefer current code, tests, workflows, README.md, tests/testing.md and docs/ over stale generated wiki text. Avoid duplicating the same material across pages: overview pages should summarize and link to focused reference pages. Do not claim a feature, transport, retry policy, authentication mechanism or deployment mode unless it exists in the repository. Use exact file paths and source-backed statements, and call out upstream-service limitations separately from project defects. Do not document .devin/wiki.json itself as a runtime component.
